scenes.line1: How does TCP start and end?
scenes.say: How does a TCP connection actually start and end? And what do all those connection states mean?
The handshake is three steps: client sends SYN, server replies with SYN-ACK, client sends ACK. Now, the connection is established.
To close, each side sends FIN and ACK. The side that closes first waits in TIME_WAIT. If you see RST, that's an abrupt reset—no waiting.

scenes.title: Check TCP states
scenes.say: You can see TCP states with this command. Lots of CLOSE_WAIT? The app isn't closing sockets. Lots of SYN_SENT? It can't reach the destination.

scenes.question: What does a RST after SYN mean?
scenes.right: It means nothing is listening, or it was rejected.
scenes.say: Watch out: if you get a RST after sending SYN, it means nothing is listening or the connection was rejected—not established.
